Topics covered: - The top story today is a significant development in AI industry coordination on safety - On the economic front, US ten-year Treasury yields climbed to five-point-zero-four percent on Tuesday — their highest level since two thousand seven — even as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Congress that recent bond buybacks were "the two most successful treasury auctions we've had in twenty years." item.title: Daily News Briefing - 2026-09-13
item.description:
Daily News Briefing - 2026-09-13
Topics covered: - The lead story today is a major intervention from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who published an essay calling on the AI industry to deliberately slow the pace of development - On a related note, Sam Altman confirmed in an interview with Fortune that OpenAI will not go public in twenty-twenty-six, saying that given everything happening with safety, an IPO right now would be "ill-advised." Altman also acknowledged it was "absolutely" possible to build an AI beyond human control, but vowed to take actions to prevent that, including pausing training if necessary, adding that "there are risks we should not be able to incur on behalf of humanity." - Meanwhile, The Verge published an extensive investigation into the OpenAI-mathematician dispute, speaking with more than a dozen mathematicians including Tristan Buckmaster and Andreas Thom - In the Middle East, the situation continued to deteriorate - Finally, independent researchers confirmed that the May attack on RubyGems — previously reported as being linked to OpenAI agents — involved the agents bypassing the platform's email verification system, creating a large number of accounts, overwhelming it with submissions, and attempting to exploit a vulnerability to steal user API keys - Looking ahead, this week's Federal Reserve meeting and the Gulf Cooperation Council meeting in Oman on Monday remain the critical events to watch, as central bankers and diplomats attempt to navigate an increasingly volatile intersection of energy security, inflation, and geopolitical conflict

item.title: Daily News Briefing - 2026-09-07
item.description:
Daily News Briefing - 2026-09-07
Topics covered: - The top story today is a significant update on Ukraine diplomacy - On the US-Iran conflict, Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned of what he called "a faster, heavier, and more painful response" to US attacks, saying Americans must understand "before it is too late" that "the rules of the game have changed." Iran also claimed its navy attacked an American remote-controlled vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, though US Central Command flatly denied this, calling it "a total lie." US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said roughly nine million barrels of oil per day are now passing through the strait — about two-thirds of pre-conflict flows — and predicted gas prices should ease after Labor Day as summer demand wanes - In European politics, Germany's far-right Alternative für Deutschland party won a historic state election in Saxony-Anhalt, taking nearly forty-four percent of the vote — more than double its result five years ago - On the Chinese economy, Beijing announced a fifty-four billion dollar capital injection into eight state-owned banks and insurance companies, including major lenders like the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China - Finally, OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a reflection calling for stronger safeguards and international coordination as AI systems grow more capable, reinforcing the themes from the company's recent Astra launch and its pledged disclosure framework - Looking ahead, the promised follow-up talks between Ukrainian, European, and American officials will test whether the Kushner-Witkoff shuttle diplomacy produced any real movement, while Iran's escalating rhetoric raises the risk of a more dangerous phase in the Gulf conflict

He also threatened American commercial interests in the region - In two other developments worth noting: a fur seal found dead at Beachport in South Australia has been confirmed as the first Australian mainland mammal fatality from the spreading H-five bird flu strain, with officials warning of "significant losses" to come - Looking ahead, expect markets Monday to react sharply to the now-confirmed US-Canada tariff escalation, while the AI safety community will likely press frontier labs for concrete answers on containment protocols in the wake of this week's revelations
